newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent skids into close, gas oil expiry looms.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent skids into close, gas oil expiry looms.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil fell steadily into the close on Monday, pulled lower by NYMEX gasoline futures and technical selling following Friday's sharp rise, brokers said.
December Brent hit the day's low of $22.87 per barrel at 1943 GMT, six cents below Friday's close, having spent most of the day above $23.00.
One broker expected the contract to finish near $23.00 because Dec options expire at the close.
"To some extent we are retracing the inexplicable gains of Friday," he added.
The time curve flattened considerably over the day, with January Brent falling just four cents and February maintaining a five cent gain on the day.

A threatened oil workers strike in Venezuela some time this week gave some support to the market, but brokers were unsure of how likely this was. The Labour Ministry has called a meeting between the union and the state oil company PdVSA early this week.
November gas oil had an eventful day, trading up to a high of $226.50 per tonne, before settleing at $220.50, just above the day's low and 75 cents over Friday settle.
"Gas oil was pretty strong because it's freezing on both sides of the Atlantic," a broker said, adding that Tuesday's expiry of the November contract was a central concern.
Around 500,000 tonnes is expected to be delivered into the contract and whether this material can then be sold outside the region could dominate sentiment.
December gas oil also gained 75 cents on the day, closing at $211.50 per tonne, but contracts further in the future climbed the most, with March 1997 up $2.50 at $196.50.
